facts.statement: Palaeorhincodon is an extinct genus of prehistoric whale sharks.
facts.quote: Palaeorhincodon (meaning "old Rhincodon") is an extinct genus of prehistoric whale shark

facts.statement: Its teeth have been found in warm water areas including North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa.
facts.quote: It had a similar distribution range to that of modern whale sharks, with teeth from Palaeorhincodon being found in warm water areas such as North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa.

facts.statement: Its teeth were very small, measuring only 3 millimeters in height.
facts.quote: Its teeth are very small, being only 3 millimeters in height.

facts.statement: Each jaw contained up to 300 rows of teeth.
facts.quote: There are up to 300 files of teeth in each jaw of Palaeorhincodon.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Jacques Herman described the genus Palaeorhincodon and its type species P. wardi in 1974.
facts.quote: In 1974, the paleontologist Jacques Herman described the fossil of a new genus of prehistoric whale shark, Palaeorhincodon, naming its type species, P. wardi

facts.statement: A new species, P. daouii, was named in 1997.
facts.quote: In 1997, a new previously undescribed species of this same genus, P. daouii, was named.

facts.statement: The genus currently includes three known species.
facts.quote: Since then, Palaeorhincodon has been placed as a genus having only 3 known species.

facts.statement: The genus existed from the Aalenian to the Tortonian, between 174.7 and 7.246 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Tortonian (174.7 to 7.246 million years ago)

facts.statement: It belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Researchers suggest it fed on plankton and larger pelagic animals such as small crustaceans, fish, and squid.
facts.quote: Palaeorhicodon presumedly behaved similarly to extant whale sharks, feeding on plankton and larger pelagic animals like small crustaceans, fish and squid.
